ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, in rectangle $ABCD$, points $E$ and $F$ are located on sides $BC$ and $AD$ respectively. The rectangle is folded along $EF$ such that point $B$ falls exactly on point $H$ on side $AD$. Given that the area of rectangle $ABCD$ is $16\sqrt{3}$ and $FH = 2HD$, what is the length of the crease $EF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram,\\
since folding the rectangle along EF makes point B precisely overlap with point H on edge AD, \\
thus, $AF=FG$, $\angle EHG=\angle B=\angle A=\angle G=90^\circ$, $HG=AB$, $\angle BEF=\angle FEH$,\\
since $\angle BEF+\angle FEH+\angle HEC=180^\circ$, $\angle HEC=60^\circ$,\\
thus, $\angle BEF=\angle FEH=60^\circ$,\\
since $AD\parallel BC$,\\
thus, $\angle FHE=\angle HEC=60^\circ$,\\
thus, $\triangle EFH$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
thus, $\angle FHE=60^\circ$,\\
thus, $\angle GHF=30^\circ$,\\
thus, $FG=\frac{1}{2}FH$,\\
since $FH=2HD$,\\
thus, $DH=FG=AF$,\\
let $DH=FG=AF=x$,\\
thus, $AB=HG=\sqrt{3}x$, $AD=4x$,\\
since the area of rectangle ABCD is $16\sqrt{3}$,\\
thus, $\sqrt{3}x \cdot 4x = 16\sqrt{3}$,\\
thus, $x=2$ (negative value is discarded),\\
thus, $AB=2\sqrt{3}$,\\
Draw $FM\perp BC$ at $M$ through F,\\
then, $FM=AB=2\sqrt{3}$,\\
thus, $EF=\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}FM=\boxed{4}$,\\

In right triangle GHF, the side FG opposite 30° equals half of the hypotenuse FH, that is, FG = FH/2. The problem gives FH = 2HD, so FG = HD. Also FG = AF, therefore let HD = FG = AF = x, then FH = 2x, AD = AF + FH + HD = x + 2x + x = 4x. From the 30°-60°-90° triangle GHF, HG = √3 x, and HG = AB, so AB = √3 x. raw_record.original_question: As shown in the diagram, in rectangle $ABCD$, points $E$ and $F$ are located on sides $BC$ and $AD$ respectively. The rectangle is folded along $EF$ such that point $B$ falls exactly on point $H$ on side $AD$. Given that the area of rectangle $ABCD$ is $16\sqrt{3}$ and $FH = 2HD$, what is the length of the crease $EF$?
raw_record.answer: Solution: As shown in the diagram, since folding the rectangle along $EF$ makes point $B$ precisely overlap with point $H$ on edge $AD$, thus, $AF=FG$, $\angle EHG=\angle B=\angle A=\angle G=90^\circ$, $HG=AB$, $\angle BEF=\angle FEH$; since $\angle BEF+\angle FEH+\angle HEC=180^\circ$, $\angle HEC=60^\circ$; thus, $\angle BEF=\angle FEH=60^\circ$; since $AD\parallel BC$, thus, $\angle FHE=\angle HEC=60^\circ$; thus, $\triangle EFH$ is an equilateral triangle; thus, $\angle GHF=30^\circ$; thus, $FG=\frac{1}{2}FH$; since $FH=2HD$, thus, $DH=FG=AF$. Let $DH=FG=AF=x$, thus, $AB=HG=\sqrt{3}x$, $AD=4x$. Since the area of rectangle $ABCD$ is $16\sqrt{3}$, thus, $\sqrt{3}x \cdot 4x = 16\sqrt{3}$, thus, $x=2$ (negative value is discarded), thus, $AB=2\sqrt{3}$. Draw $FM\perp BC$ at $M$ through $F$, then, $FM=AB=2\sqrt{3}$, thus, $EF=\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}FM=\boxed{4}$.
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is rectangle ABCD, AD is the upper side, BC is the lower side, E is on BC, F and H are on AD, and F is to the left of H. The dashed-line part indicates the position before folding; the folded vertex G is located above AD, and FG, GH, HE, EF are connected. In the figure, at point E, the angle between EH and EC is marked as 60°. Reasoning: After folding along EF, point B falls onto H, so EF is the crease, the image of EB is EH, the image of BA is HG, and the image of FA is FG. Therefore ∠BEF = ∠FEH, HG = AB, FG = AF, and ∠EHG = 90°. Because B, E, C are collinear, and in the figure ∠HEC = 60°, ∠BEF + ∠FEH + ∠HEC = 180°. Also ∠BEF = ∠FEH, so the two are each 60°. Since AD ∥ BC, ∠FHE = ∠HEC = 60°. Thus two angles of triangle EFH are both 60°, so triangle EFH is an equilateral triangle, hence EF = FH. Also because ∠EHG = 90°, and ∠FHE = 60°, ∠GHF = 30°. In right triangle GHF, the side FG opposite 30° equals half of the hypotenuse FH, that is, FG = FH/2. The problem gives FH = 2HD, so FG = HD. Also FG = AF, therefore let HD = FG = AF = x, then FH = 2x, AD = AF + FH + HD = x + 2x + x = 4x. From the 30°-60°-90° triangle GHF, HG = √3 x, and HG = AB, so AB = √3 x. The area of the rectangle is AB × AD = 16√3, therefore (√3 x)(4x) = 16√3, giving x = 2. Thus FH = 2x = 4. Because EFH is an equilateral triangle, EF = FH = 4.
